title: The は particle
summary: は is not a carriage. It is a flag that says what the sentence is about, and it never changes who does what.

blocks.text: Many courses teach **は** on day one, so learners think it means "is" or "the subject". It is neither. は (read "wa" when it is a particle) can never be a black carriage, and it is not a white carriage like を. It is a **flag** that you plant on the **topic**: what the sentence is about. It does not say anything about the topic; the real sentence does that.
Because は is not a logical particle, the sentence underneath still needs its own main carriage and が (often a zero).
私は学生だ。 Literally: "As for me, (I) am a student."

blocks.en: As for me, (I) am a student.

blocks.text: A famous puzzle: 「私はうなぎだ」 does **not** mean "I am an eel". At a restaurant the zero carriage is the **dish**, not the speaker: "As for me, (it) is eel," so "I'll have the eel." The topic flag shapes which zero you hear.

blocks.en: As for me, (it) is eel: I'll have the eel.

blocks.text: The logical particles decide who does what

**が** marks the doer, **を** marks what is done to, and **に** marks the **target** it is aimed at. Because these three fix the roles, word order is flexible. Even a silly sentence stays grammatical: the particles decide.

blocks.jp: 私がさくらにボールを投げる。
blocks.en: I throw the ball to Sakura.

blocks.jp: さくらに私がボールを投げる。
blocks.en: I throw the ball to Sakura. (same roles, different order)

blocks.jp: ボールがさくらを私に投げる。
blocks.en: The ball throws Sakura to me. (nonsense, but perfectly grammatical)

blocks.text: Moving は changes emphasis, never logic
Changing a logical particle changes the event. Moving the は flag only changes what you are talking about.

blocks.jp: 私はさくらにボールを投げる。
blocks.en: As for me, I throw the ball to Sakura.

blocks.jp: ボールは私がさくらに（ゼロを）投げる。
blocks.en: As for the ball, I throw (it) to Sakura.

items: **は** flags the **topic**. It says nothing about it.
は is not a main carriage and not a white carriage.
The sentence under the topic still has its own が, often a zero.
**が・を・に** decide who does what to whom. Moving **は** never changes that.

questions.note: は plants a flag on the topic and says nothing more.

questions.note: は is only a topic flag; the sentence below it keeps its own が.

questions.note: は flags the topic: the ball.
が marks the doer: 私. The topic is the ball, but I am the one throwing.

questions.note: に marks the target of the action.

questions.instruction: Which sentence means "Sakura throws the ball to me"?
options: さくらが私にボールを投げる
私がさくらにボールを投げる
ボールがさくらを私に投げる
私にボールがさくらを投げる
questions.note: さくら is marked が (the doer) and 私 is marked に (the target).

options: As for me, (I) am a student
questions.note: は introduces the topic; 学生だ is the real sentence.

questions.instruction: Which of these is a logical particle (it decides who does what)?
questions.note: が, を and に are logical. は and も only flag topics.

questions.prompt: ボールがさくらを私に投げる is grammatical, but it means the ball throws Sakura to me.
questions.note: The particles fix the roles, so the sentence is grammatical, even if the scene is silly.
